reading: Independently viewed final printed pages1112,1120,1122 and corrected author pages3,9,11. Read final introduction concerning nondegeneracy after maximal divisible quotient. Read the source comparison and current main1791–1808 plus the complete proposed assertion and connection.
reasoning: Corollary4 identifies the obstruction with Pic^(g-1). For the genus-one curve E this is Pic^0, whose rational identity trivializes the torsor. Hence c=0; Corollary7 gives alternation for this actual polarization.

Nondegeneracy is on the quotient by the maximal divisible subgroup. The supplied decomposition of the2-primary group as D direct sum F identifies D as maximal: the image of a divisible subgroup in the finite quotient is a finite divisible group and is zero. Different primary components are orthogonal because their pairing values have coprime annihilators. Therefore nondegeneracy restricts to F.

A finite alternating nondegenerate2-primary pairing splits into paired cyclic factors by choosing an element of maximal order and a partner with primitive pairing value, splitting off the resulting hyperbolic pair, and repeating. In particular dim F[2] is even. Theorem8(3) also gives this square-cardinality assertion directly. No nondegeneracy of the restricted pairing on F[2] is used.

Combining the supplied finite Kummer dimension relation with t+dim F[2]=dim Sha[2] leaves r+t+dim F[2]=1. The even nonnegative last term is zero, and a finite2-group with no2-torsion is trivial. Thus F=0 and r+t=1, conditional on the separately supplied decomposition and Kummer inputs.

The published1999 notation incorrectly identifies maximal divisible membership with individual divisibility for an arbitrary group. The2014 author text adds finiteness of M[p]. Current main1803–1804 explicitly avoids the arbitrary-group identification and instead proves maximality from the actual decomposition. The relevant Corollaries4,7 and Theorem8 statements agree across versions.
